- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment — increase forecast lows to avoid excessive downward bias.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes — apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce it; if below, raise it.
- Sentiment reversal triggers correction: if sentiment turns from negative to positive, reduce forecast slope; if positive to negative, increase downward pressure.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early-term decline — adjust downward for days 1–7 if sentiment is negative.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — don’t mirror sentiment history exactly; dampen sentiment-driven volatility in forecasts.
